cover.title: Plastic waste on coastal shores
cover.subtitle: Plastic waste litters beaches and fills fishing nets in Sierra Leone. Discover how density helps measure plastic pollution in the ocean.

cover.fun_fact: Over 72,000 pieces of litter were recorded across four coastal beaches.
story.title: Catching more plastic than fish
story.lead: On coastal beaches in Sierra Leone, fishers haul in nets filled with plastic bottles and water sachets instead of fish [1]. Plastic waste disrupts daily fishing work and increases operating expenses [1].
story.image_credit: Mandeiya flower / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

stat.3.label: annual metric tons of plastic waste
story.body_1: Fisher Sheriff Kamara finds single-use plastics caught in his nets almost every week [1]. Removing entangled plastic waste takes considerable time, causing delayed catches and added repair costs [1]. International environmental reports highlight how marine plastic threatens aquatic life and coastal communities [2].
story.body_2: Women fish traders also bear financial burdens when fresh fish deliveries are delayed and ice or firewood expenses rise [1]. Managing plastic waste requires stronger coastal waste management systems and community cleanup efforts [1] [2].
timeline.1.text: Fishers set out to sea in boats powered by petrol.
timeline.2.text: Nets haul in plastic bottles and wrappers alongside fish.
timeline.3.text: Traders process fish and clean nets from debris.
physics.title: Density and material properties
physics.body_1: Density tells us how much mass is packed into a specific volume. Different materials have different densities, determining whether they float or sink in water.
physics.body_2: Measuring density helps scientists and environmental groups analyze plastic waste accumulation in coastal ecosystems [2].
physics.assumptions: We assume uniform mass distribution and regular volume measurements for solid objects.

lab.title: Density test: sink or float?
lab.step_1: Fill a transparent container with clean water.
lab.step_2: Drop a small plastic bottle and a metal spoon into the water.
lab.step_3: Observe which object floats and which object sinks.
lab.question: Why did the plastic bottle float while the spoon sank?
